Purpose: interview of eyewitness to the 07/15/2026 CTA bus #1342 collision at Pulaski Rd & Peterson Ave, Chicago. Interview scheduled at our office 10/08/2026. Objective: a signed, dated written statement and his agreement to be contacted by counsel.

## Opening (identify honestly - no pretext)
"Mr. Fields, thanks for coming in. My name is ____, a licensed investigator with Ridgeline Investigative Group in Chicago - we spoke on the phone last Sunday. I'm working with the law firm Bellamy & Sorensen, who represent the driver whose car was hit by the CTA bus at Pulaski and Peterson back on July 15th. You told me you saw the bus run the red light. Before we start, do you have about twenty minutes?"
- If he asks why we're involved: "Our firm was hired to locate witnesses. You're free to talk to us or not, and you can stop at any time."
- Get his consent ON THE RECORD before any recording: "Is it all right with you if I record our conversation so I don't misquote you?" (Illinois requires the consent of all parties to record - 720 ILCS 5/14-2. If he declines, take written notes only.)

## Identity / foundation questions
1. "For the record, can you confirm your full name and date of birth?"
2. "Where do you live currently?" (Confirm 6588 N Talbrook Ave, Chicago.)
3. "What's the best phone number to reach you? The number on the police report doesn't work anymore." (Open item - capture the updated number.)
4. "Where do you work, and what's your schedule like?" (Confirms City of Chicago Streets & Sanitation, Logan Square yard - and the best time to reach him.)

## Accident observations (open-ended first, then specifics)
5. "In your own words, tell me what you saw that day." (Let him talk; do not lead.)
6. "Where were you sitting on the bus, and where were you looking just before the impact?"
7. "What did you see the bus do as it approached the intersection? What color was the light for the bus? What color was it for the other car?"
8. "Did you notice the bus's speed? Was it slowing down, or maintaining speed?"
9. "What did you hear - horns, brakes, the driver saying anything before or after?"
10. "What happened at the moment of impact? Where were you thrown, and were you hurt?"
11. "What happened right after - what did the driver do, what did passengers do?"
12. "Did you speak to the responding officer? Do you remember telling him the bus ran the red light? What exactly did you say?"
13. "Did anyone else on the bus say they saw it? Do you remember any names or descriptions?"
14. "Did you speak with anyone from the CTA, the police, or any insurance company afterward? Did anyone take your statement or ask you not to talk?"
15. "Is there anything about traffic that day - weather, sun glare, construction, signals out - that matters?"
16. "Have you ever been a passenger on that route before? Do you know that intersection?"

## Wrap-up
17. "Would you be willing to sign a short written summary of what you just told me?" (Read it back to him; correct in his own words; sign and date both pages.)
18. "Counsel may need to talk with you and may ask you to appear if this goes further. Is it all right if they contact you at [the number he gave]?" Get a signed contact-release if he agrees.
19. "Is there anything I haven't asked that you think matters?"
20. Thank him; give him the investigator's direct line and the firm's card; tell him he can call with corrections at any time.

## Rules for the interviewer
- Do NOT discuss settlement, damages, the value of the claim, or who is at fault beyond his own observations.
- Do NOT offer or imply any payment, gift or benefit for his statement or testimony.
- Do NOT record without his express consent; do not photograph or video him in the office without consent.
- Do NOT coach, suggest answers, or correct his account - record it as he states it.

- Refer all legal questions ("Do I have to testify?", "Can I get in trouble?") to counsel; do not give legal advice.

{"content": "# Call script - RIG-2026-1011 - initial contact with Pamela J. Kroger (née Haugen), heir in estate #E-3392 (D. Navarro / assigned investigator)

Use once the subject is located and a current phone number or address is in hand. Client is P. Alvarez, Esq. (Alvarez & Farris LLP), attorney for the Estate of Eleanor M. Haugen (Kenosha County Probate #E-3392). Goal: confirm identity, notify her of the estate and of her potential inheritance, and capture a current mailing address and preferred contact method.

## Before dialing
- Confirm the number is verified as hers (recent vendor data, or obtained from a record we can cite). Do not cold-dial the stale (262) numbers.
- Have ready: the estate name and number, the attorney's name and firm, the investigator's name and license, and our office number so she can call back and verify us independently.
- Recording: Illinois is an all-party consent state (720 ILCS 5/14-2). Wisconsin and Indiana are generally one-party consent, but as a matter of firm practice, ask permission before recording any call and record only with her express consent.

## Opening (honest identification - no pretext, no misrepresentation)
"Hello, is this Pamela Kroger - formerly Pamela Haugen? My name is ____, a licensed private investigator with Ridgeline Investigative Group in Chicago. I'm calling on behalf of the attorney for the estate of your aunt, Eleanor Haugen. It's not an emergency and it's not bad news about any legal claim against you - it's about her estate and a possible inheritance. Do you have a few minutes?"
- If she asks how we got her number: "From public records and estate-probate sources. I can only tell you that the estate's attorney asked us to locate family members."
- If she is suspicious: "That's completely reasonable. You can hang up and call our office, or call Mr. Alvarez at Alvarez & Farris directly - I can give you his number."
- If she says "not interested" or asks not to be contacted: "Understood. I'll note that in the file and no one from this office will call you again. Before I go - the court may still need to reach you by mail; may I confirm the last mailing address you have on file?" Then end the call politely and document it.

## Identity confirmation (gentle, two or three items only)
1. "Can you confirm your maiden name was Haugen?"
2. "And that Eleanor Haugen of Kenosha was your aunt?"
3. "Thank you - I just have to be sure I've reached the right person."

## Substance (keep it factual; do not give legal advice or valuations)
4. "Ms. Haugen passed away, and her estate is being administered in Kenosha County probate, case number E-3392. The attorney for the estate, Mr. Alvarez, needs to reach you because you may be an heir/beneficiary."
5. "I'm not able to tell you what the estate is worth or what your share might be - and I wouldn't want to guess. Mr. Alvarez can walk you through all of that."
6. "The court sent a certified letter to your old address on Vinehaven Trail in Racine and it came back undeliverable, which is why the attorney hired us to find you."
7. "Would you like me to have Mr. Alvarez's office contact you directly? What's the best number and time?"
8. "And what mailing address should the attorney and the court use for you?"

## Close-out
9. Confirm and read back: current mailing address, best phone, preferred contact method (phone/mail/email), and whether she consents to the attorney contacting her directly.
10. "Thank you. One last thing - if you'd rather not be involved, that's your choice, and Mr. Alvarez can explain what that means. He can also answer any legal questions - I can't."
11. Document the call immediately: date, time, number dialed, what was said, her responses, consent/refusal, and any new addresses obtained. Upload to the case file for counsel.

## Rules
- Do NOT state or imply an inheritance amount, a percentage, or a guaranteed distribution.
- Do NOT ask for a Social Security number, bank account, date of birth or other financial identifiers on this call - the attorney handles any identity/probate documentation.
- Do NOT pressure her to act, sign, or send anything. Beware of anything that resembles an "advance-fee inheritance" pitch; our contact must clearly not resemble one - hence the full identification and the offer to verify us independently.
- Do NOT discuss other family members, the decedent's affairs, or disputes within the family.
- If she has counsel of her own, take the attorney's name and number and route all further contact through them.
- If a different person answers, leave no details beyond your name, firm, and callback number.

- Get his consent ON THE RECORD before any recording: "Is it all right with you if I record our conversation so I don't misquote you?" (Illinois requires the consent of all parties to record - 720 ILCS 5/14-2. If he declines, take written notes only.)

## Identity / foundation questions
1. "For the record, can you confirm your full name and date of birth?"
2. "Where do you live currently?" (Confirm 6588 N Talbrook Ave, Chicago.)

5. "In your own words, tell me what you saw that day." (Let him talk; do not lead.)
6. "Where were you sitting on the bus, and where were you looking just before the impact?"
7. "What did you see the bus do as it approached the intersection? What color was the light for the bus? What color was it for the other car?"
8. "Did you notice the bus's speed? Was it slowing down, or maintaining speed?"

13. "Did anyone else on the bus say they saw it? Do you remember any names or descriptions?"
14. "Did you speak with anyone from the CTA, the police, or any insurance company afterward? Did anyone take your statement or ask you not to talk?"
15. "Is there anything about traffic that day - weather, sun glare, construction, signals out - that matters?"
16. "Have you ever been a passenger on that route before? Do you know that intersection?"

17. "Would you be willing to sign a short written summary of what you just told me?" (Read it back to him; correct in his own words; sign and date both pages.)
